column2: Fortnum & Mason has been at 181 Piccadilly since 1707. Above the door, figures of the two founders bow to each other.
Hatchards has sold books on Piccadilly since 1797. That's a lot of books through one address.
Fouquet's opened in 1899. The name has been on the Champs-Élysées for over a century.
Le Procope opened as a café in 1686 and closed in 1872. The present restaurant dates from 1957.
Botín is at Calle de Cuchilleros 17. Guinness lists it as the world's oldest restaurant.
San Ginés opened in 1894. You can also find it in writing by Galdós and Valle-Inclán.
Two Englishwomen opened Babington's beside the Spanish Steps in 1893. That explains the English name.
Demel became a court confectioner in 1874. Its cake has carried the 'Eduard-Sacher-Torte' seal since 1963.
U Fleků has been at Křemencova 11 since 1499. The address hasn't needed much updating.
Café Louvre opened in 1902. Kafka, Einstein and Karel Čapek all spent time here.
Kugler moved here in 1870. Emil Gerbeaud joined in 1884; his is the name on the café now.
New York Café opened in 1894. There's a story that writers threw the door key into the Danube to keep it open. A legend, though.
Michail Brettos opened Brettos in Plaka in 1909. The founder's name is still above the door.
KaDeWe opened on 27 March 1907. A very specific date behind a familiar Berlin name.
Max Konnopke began selling sausages in 1930. This stand opened in 1960.
Neuhaus started here as a pharmacy in 1857. Jean Neuhaus created the praline in 1912. Different contents behind the counter.
In January 2004, Delirium Café entered Guinness with 2,004 beer brands on its list. The number and year are easy to mix up.
Café Hoppe dates from 1670. Number 18 is known as the 'standing Hoppe'. The name is fairly literal.
Tivoli opened in 1843. Its wooden roller coaster came along in 1914. Quite a gap between the two.
Den Gyldene Freden opened in 1722. Carl Michael Bellman helped make its name familiar through his songs.
Bewley's has been on Grafton Street since 1927. The stained-glass windows are by Harry Clarke.
The Brazen Head traces its history to 1198. It turns up in James Joyce's Ulysses too.
Wedel began in 1851 and moved its main factory to Szpitalna in 1894. Two dates behind that address.
The kafana called '?' has used that name since 1892. One character is enough for the sign.
Travellers left messages on an acacia's thorns at the Stanley's Thorn Tree Café. Easy to see how the café got its name.
Shibuya 109 opened in April 1979. Read 10 as 'tō' and 9 as 'kyū' and the name becomes Tōkyū.
Jay Fai, at 327 Maha Chai Road, received a star in the first Michelin Guide Bangkok. The goggles are hers too.
Raffles opened in 1887. The hotel has kept its name through more than a century of changes around it.
Café Batavia is in a building from around the 1830s on Fatahillah Square. The building came first, the café later.
Café Tortoni dates from 1858. Borges had a regular table here; a wax figure of him now keeps that connection visible.
La Puerta Falsa opened on 16 July 1816. A small doorway with a long history.
Myeongdong Kyoja opened as Jangsujang in 1966 and took its current name in 1978. It entered Michelin Guide Seoul in 2017.
The first BeaverTails stand opened in the ByWard Market in 1980. This is where that part of the story starts.
Old Ebbitt Grill dates from 1856. It calls itself Washington's oldest bar; Grant and Andrew Johnson were regular visitors.
Hacı Bekir, Bahçekapı'da küçük bir dükkânla başlamış. Yıl 1777. Adını bilince tarihini de merak ediyor insan.
Pandeli 1901'e uzanıyor. Mısır Çarşısı girişinin üstündeki mavi çinili yer.
Vefa Bozacısı 1876'dan beri burada. Atatürk'ün boza içtiği bardak da vitrinde sergileniyor.
Hacı Abdullah'ın hikâyesi 1888'de Karaköy'de başlamış. Bugünkü adını bilip başlangıcını bilmemek kolay.
Pera Palace 1895'te Orient Express yolcuları için açılmış. Otelin hikâyesinin bir ucu trene çıkıyor.
